threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver yells 'next stop!' instead of just saying it. Locals just nod and hold on tight.
Last night on the 133, a guy started singing 'No Woman, No Cry' loudly, and by the end, half the bus was clapping along like it was a concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The first time I saw a guy in shorts waiting for a bus while it snowed. That’s when I knew I was really home in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a club that opens at 6 AM, celebrates daytime raves, and serves genuine Döner to the sleep-deprived.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their quick sidestep when a BART delay announcement interrupts their flow. Tourists just stand there, looking helpless.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing violin at Mission & 24th, Muni bus honked, and he played off the rhythm like it was part of the show. Classic SF magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into a bar and expect to chat for hours. In Gràcia, it’s more about a quick caña and moving on.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones trying to order a ‘café con leche’ before 10am, still unaware it's ‘café amb llet’ here in Gràcia.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground' when you're stuck on a train at Dalston Junction.
Caught a night bus last week, and a group of guys tried to sing 'Wonderwall.' One guy just said he’d rather listen to the driver’s playlist.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid selling lemonade on the corner while a busker played a sax solo nearby—so quintessentially Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous barbecues in parks here, or DJ sets on the banks of the Spree—it's like the city throws a party just because it's sunny.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local if they’ve got a favorite taco spot that doesn't have a line at 2am. Tourists are still looking for La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, saw a guy juggling on the 19 Polk, while a woman ordered takeout on her phone. Just another Tuesday in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the locals live in cafes all day, but most of us are juggling work and family, squeezing in a quick café amb llet before the next commitment.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: Recent arrivals often order café con leche at night, totally oblivious to the locals sipping vermut instead. It's a dead giveaway.
